hook.line: A lot of you would crush if you made a video saying 'hey, I'm Paul'.
hook.visual: Speaker in a cap on a dark stage, gesturing mid-sentence; white-and-yellow title 'THE BEST WAY TO GET NEW CLIENTS' up top; big word captions pop at mid-frame, 'crush' scaled up.

beats.what: Stage clip opens mid-thought under a two-line yellow/white title promising the best way to get clients
Key word 'crush' pops in much larger than the other caption words
Cut to a tighter angle as he role-plays the agent's intro video ('Hey, I'm Sara' shown as a quote)
Small italic disclaimer appears: talking to real estate agents, but works for many
The tactic: an email in the video, a dinner every two weeks for six to eight people
Quick cutaway to him at a bar with wine bottles on 'wine dinner'
Rapid cuts between angles as he lists golf, run club
Cutaway to a pickleball court on the swear-word punchline
Back on stage for the moral: use digital to go analog, stay honest

why_it_works: Starts mid-sentence on 'you would crush', so the first word is a payoff aimed at the viewer, not a warm-up
Concrete, copyable tactic (an email in the video, a paid dinner every two weeks) beats generic advice; viewers can picture doing it
Literal b-roll cutaways on each example (wine bar, pickleball court) reward the list with a new picture, speeding up the back half
Live-audience stage setting lends authority and energy without any graphics work
weaknesses: First 28 s are one long stage shot (longest shot 23.7 s), all the visual change is crammed into the last third
Caption sits over his torso and 81% of text is outside the safe area
Ends abruptly mid-sentence with no on-screen call to action; the share ask only lives in the caption
for_robert: Use one literal cutaway per example in a list: when he names 'wine dinner' or 'pickleball', cut to a matching picture (or Fred dressed for it) for one second, then back to his face.
